sections.h2: What must a Rockaway homeowner finish before closing?
sections.html:
Rockaway Borough's sheet on selling a home lists three items due before closing: a Certificate of Compliance for Fire Prevention, a final water reading, and property taxes paid in full. Each has its own office and its own fee, so start all three as soon as you have a contract.

This page covers Rockaway Borough in Morris County, a 2.07 square mile municipality of 6,598 residents at the 2020 census. The Census Bureau estimates 6,631 for July 2025, up 0.8 percent from its 2020 base. Rockaway Township borders the borough and is a separate municipality with its own offices, so confirm which one holds your address before you call anyone.

The borough has a mayor and six council members, with council seats staggered so that two are elected each year. Zoning questions go to the borough zoning officer by email at Zoning@rockawayborough.org, and the zoning office takes appointments through 973-627-2000, extension 229.

sections.h2: How does the Rockaway fire prevention certificate work?
sections.html:
The Bureau of Fire Prevention issues the certificate, and you schedule by calling 973-625-3473 (973-625-FIRE) and leaving your name, address and phone number. Staff answer on weekdays, with a 4:30 p.m. close. The borough's sheet is dated October 1, 2022, and it sets the fee by how early you ask.

  • 10 or more business days before closing: $55 for the first inspection.
  • 4 to 10 business days before closing: $90.
  • Fewer than 4 business days before closing: $200.
  • Any later inspection: $40.

The sheet asks for a working smoke detector on each level including the basement, a carbon monoxide detector on each level that has bedrooms, no open building permits, and a house number at least 4 inches tall. It also lists a portable extinguisher, but state law removed that item from resale inspections in February 2025, so ask the bureau what it checks now. A house with a monitored fire alarm needs a test report dated within 12 months and someone present who can reset the panel.

sections.h2: What are the final water reading and trash rules for a Rockaway sale?
sections.html:
Call the Water Clerk at 973-627-2000, extension 223, for the final reading. The fee in the borough sheet is $60 with 72 hours or more of notice and $95 with less.

For clean-out, a single-family house may set out three 32-gallon cans plus three bulk items each week. Condominiums and townhouses arrange their own collection of large items. For anything beyond that, hire a hauler, because a vacant inherited house can hold more than curbside service will take.

The Construction Office, reached at 973-627-8035 on weekdays, handles the open permit check. Rockaway's property maintenance article requires a certificate of continued occupancy to sell or lease, but that article says it applies to nonresidential and mixed-occupancy buildings and not to residential structures, so a house is not swept into it.

sections.h2: How do Rockaway's numbers compare with the national average?
sections.html:
Rockaway is a stable, mid-priced borough where few households move in any one year. The table uses Census QuickFacts estimates for 2020 to 2024, except retail sales, which are from 2022.

Rockaway borough against the United States, Census QuickFacts
MeasureRockawayUnited States
Stayed at the same address over 12 months97.1%87.7%
Typical owner-occupied home value$448,100$332,700
Monthly owner costs with a mortgage$2,949$1,963
Retail sales per resident, 2022$62,635$20,928
Residents below the poverty line6.2%10.2%

There are 2,711 households averaging 2.43 people, and owners hold 60.4 percent of homes. Median household income is $107,053, and 24.9 percent of residents age five and older speak another language at home.

The 2020 census counted 2,645 housing units in the borough, of which 3.2 percent were vacant, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.9 percent and a rental vacancy rate of 4.6 percent. The median age was 42.2, and 16.0 percent of residents were 65 or older. With so few empty owner-occupied homes, buyers have little to choose from, and older owners mean estate and downsizing sales make up part of what does come up.

Rockaway became a borough on June 19, 1894, carved from Rockaway Township after a referendum held the day before, and took in more township land in 1908. The name matches the Rockaway River and has been said to mean place of sands, creek between two hills, or bushy.

The First Presbyterian Church of Rockaway was founded in 1758, its cemetery holds many Revolutionary War veterans, and the current brick church dates to 1832. The borough's population reached 6,852 in 1980, dipped to 6,243 in 1990, and has hovered near 6,500 since 2000, which fits the low turnover in the table above.. Main Street and the Mill Lane Tavern appear in the 2003 film The Station Agent, which was shot in the borough.

The climate is a hot-summer humid continental type, so a house here faces hot humid summers and moderately cold winters.

sections.h2: Which roads, buses and schools serve Rockaway?
sections.html:
The borough has 25.88 miles of roads, 20.16 of them municipal. Interstate 80 clips the northeast corner, reached from Exit 37 on County Route 513, and U.S. Route 46 crosses the south end. NJ Transit trains do not stop in Rockaway, but the Denville and Dover stations are close, on the Morris and Essex and Montclair-Boonton lines. NJ Transit local bus 880 serves the borough, and Lakeland Bus Lines runs Route 46 and Route 80 service along Main Street to Port Authority.

  • Rockaway Borough Public Schools teach prekindergarten through grade 8: Lincoln Elementary (PreK-3) and Thomas Jefferson Middle School (4-8), with 574 students in 2024 to 2025.
  • High school students go to Morris Hills High School, which sits in the borough and belongs to the Morris Hills Regional High School District.
  • Divine Mercy Academy, opened in 2016, is the borough's only private school.

sections.h2: How do Morris County tax appeals and estate sales work for a Rockaway house?
sections.html:
The Morris County Board of Taxation, at P.O. Box 900, Morristown, holds appeal hearings in person only. Its guidance says an assessment is excessive only if it fails one of two standards: full market value as of the prior October 1 in a revaluation year, or the municipality's common level range in other years. Ask the board for the Rockaway filing date for the tax year you care about.

If you inherited the house, an executor signs the deed and the New Jersey GIT/REP form. A New Jersey estate uses the GIT/REP-3, and an executor who is also a beneficiary signs two forms. At the borough's $448,100 median value, the state transfer fee comes to about $3,677 when each rate band is applied to the slice of price inside it.

faqs.q: Who issues the resale certificate in Rockaway Borough?
faqs.a: The Bureau of Fire Prevention. Call 973-625-3473 to schedule, and expect fees from $55 to $200 depending on how close to closing you book, according to the borough's October 2022 sheet.

faqs.q: Does Rockaway require a certificate of continued occupancy for a house sale?
faqs.a: The borough's property maintenance article requires one for nonresidential and mixed buildings and says it does not apply to residential structures. Ask the Construction Office at 973-627-8035 whether anything else applies to your address.

faqs.q: How do I get a final water reading in Rockaway?
faqs.a: Contact the Water Clerk at 973-627-2000, extension 223. The borough sheet lists $60 with at least 72 hours of notice and $95 on shorter notice.

faqs.q: Is Rockaway Borough the same as Rockaway Township?
faqs.a: No. They are separate Morris County municipalities with separate offices, and the borough was split off from the township in 1894. Check your tax bill to see which one you are in.

faqs.q: What does the state transfer fee cost on a typical Rockaway sale?
faqs.a: About $3,677 at the borough's $448,100 median home value. The seller owes it at recording, and the amount rises with the price.
